beats.say: Right now, your internet is a stream of tiny flashes of light, racing through glass.
Inside the cable is a strand of glass as thin as a human hair. That is the whole road.
Your message is turned into on and off flashes. Light on is a one. Light off is a zero.
The flashes bounce along the inside of the glass, like light in a long mirrored tunnel, and they stay trapped inside.
The glass is so clear that the light can travel a very long way before it fades.
On really long routes, boosters give the light a fresh push along the way.
Different colours of light can share the same strand at once, so one hair of glass carries many streams.
And why so fast? Nothing travels faster than light, and these flashes can switch on and off incredibly quickly.
At the far end, a receiver turns the flashes back into your video, your page, your message.
Follow for how things work, in a minute.
